newsitem.title: UK: BT shares rise after $20 billion U.S. deal.
newsitem.headline: BT shares rise after $20 billion U.S. deal.

text.p: Shares in British Telecom Plc rose sharply in heavy trading on Monday after Sunday's confirmation of the group's planned $20 billion merger with MCI Communications of the United States.

BT was up 24p at 375 shortly after the start of trading, with trading volume reaching over six million shares. The rise in BT -- one of Britain's biggest companies -- also helped push the FTSE 100 index of leading shares up 7.5 points to 3,956.0.

Despite the huge cost of the deal to BT -- it will be the biggest-ever acquisition by a British firm -- the merger is seen as having a compelling industrial logic, linking leading phone companies on both sides of the Atlantic.
For BT shareholders the deal is also being sugared with a promise of a special one-off 35p dividend payout and a higher rate of general dividend increases in the future.

"It is positive for BT shareholders and positive for the (telecoms) sector," said Jim McCafferty, analyst at broking house ABN AMRO Hoare Govett. Under the terms of the acquisition, which is still to be approved by regulators on both sides of the Atlantic, BT is paying more than $20 billion in cash and shares for the 80 percent of MCI which is does not already own.

The deal will create the second-largest phone company in the world after Japan's NTT, giving a fresh impetus to global telecoms competition and offering the posibility of lower international phone charges.
Announcing details of the transaction yesterday, BT chairman Sir Ian Vallance said: "This is not a pebble we're throwing onto a quiet pool. It is a big rock, and it's going to make a big splash."
